prTitle: Implement access token context encoding framework
head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696

tps.bug: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
tps.evidenciaOpus: AccessTokenContext.java:73 (diff line 184) calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), validating grantType twice and never rawTokenId, so a null raw id is accepted and encodeTokenId emits '...:null'.
tps.evidenciaAstra: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 checks grantType again, then assigns rawTokenId without validation at line 77. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:117 concatenates that value, so a null raw ID is accepted and serialized as ':null'.

tps.bug: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
tps.evidenciaOpus: AssertEvents.java:480-484 reads items[0].substring(3,5) although the encoder puts the grant at [4,6) (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider substring(4,6)), and returns false on equality; for valid ids the slice never equals the shortcut, so the matcher only checks the UUID and never verifies the grant.
tps.evidenciaAstra: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 uses substring(3,5) and rejects equality, whereas services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:81 extracts substring(4,6). Consequently, the matcher accepts wrong-grant IDs with valid UUID suffixes, leaving the intended grant assertions ineffective.

tps.bug: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
tps.evidenciaOpus: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:77-83 catches RuntimeException; the fixture never calls postInit so sessionFactory is null, and 'ac' is not in the map, so getGrantTypeByShortcut hits sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream and throws NullPointerException instead of the decoder's IllegalArgumentException; the test passes for the wrong reason.
tps.evidenciaAstra: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:40 initializes the factory without postInit and supplies maps without 'ac'; line 82 accepts any RuntimeException. The lookup therefore dereferences the unset sessionFactory in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:125, allowing the test to pass without exercising the intended unknown-grant validation.

tps.bug: Client-credentials (and UMA permission) token issuance never sets the GRANT_TYPE attribute, so their access token ids are encoded with the unknown grant 'na' instead of their shortcut.
tps.evidenciaOpus: Only OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, the password grant, refresh, pre-authorized code and token exchange set Constants.GRANT_TYPE; ClientCredentialsGrantType (lines 121-141) builds its own clientSessionCtx and calls responseBuilder.generateAccessToken() without it, so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider:57-60 falls back to 'na' for client-credentials tokens.
tps.evidenciaAstra: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/ClientCredentialsGrantType.java:122 creates its context and line 141 generates the token without setting the grant attribute; services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/authorization/AuthorizationTokenService.java:350 similarly creates a context before generation at line 358. Both bypass the assignment in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109, so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:57-60 records these known grants as 'na'.

tps.bug: Lazy registration of newly deployed grants does not check shortcut uniqueness, so a grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites the reverse mapping and older tokens decode to the wrong grant.
tps.evidenciaOpus: getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:106-137) lazily put new grants into both maps without the duplicate-shortcut check done in postInit, so a hot-deployed grant reusing a shortcut overwrites the reverse mapping.
tps.evidenciaAstra: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 overwrites the reverse mapping during lazy registration while line 114 retains the new forward mapping alongside existing entries. Unlike the startup validation at line 82, this path does not reject collisions, so registering another grant with the same shortcut changes how earlier tokens decode.

tps.bug: getShortcut() is added as an abstract method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default, breaking existing custom grant type factories (compile error or AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it).
tps.evidenciaOpus: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29-33 adds `String getShortcut();` with no default to the provider factory interface, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 calls gtf.getShortcut() for every deployed grant factory. Only built-in factories were updated, so third-party grant type factories fail to compile or hit AbstractMethodError at postInit.
tps.evidenciaAstra: The PR adds abstract getShortcut() without a default in server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33, breaking compilation of existing custom implementations lacking it. services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-76 unconditionally calls it on every registered grant factory during postInit, so previously compiled implementations can throw AbstractMethodError and prevent startup.
